subject: Renewal: BlueHarbor — EU launch + APAC warm-standby and capacity addendum
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@blueharborhealth.com>
Cc: procurement@blueharborhealth.com
Date: 2026-09-29T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal: BlueHarbor — EU launch + APAC warm-standby and capacity addendum

Hi Emma,

Thanks again for the productive call last week. As we approach the end of your current term (Nov 30), I wanted to surface a clear proposal so legal and procurement have something to review early. High-level: BlueHarbor is asking to (1) expand primary serving into an EU region, (2) add an APAC warm-standby node for failover/traffic seeding, and (3) increase committed capacity for Q1–Q4 next year.

Proposed commercial/term changes:
- Move from 12-month to 24-month term (aligns pricing and committed capacity).
- Add a 30% committed capacity uplift on the existing Dedicated pool (details and pricing in attached SOW draft).
- EU node will be treated as "primary" for EU traffic; APAC will be configured as warm-standby with automated cross-region failover.

Questions for you so we can finalize the draft addendum:
1) Do you need EU primary to be in a specific country (DE/FR/IE)?
2) Any minimum encryption/HSM/KMS constraints for EU or APAC?
3) Target throughput for EU day-1 (rps or tokens/sec) and target failover RPS for APAC?

Next steps I propose: Ben (solutions) and Marissa (account lead) will provide a technical runbook and capacity estimate by EOD Thu; I’ll send a redlined addendum for procurement thereafter. Could we lock a 30-minute slot early next week (Oct 4–5) for signoff?

Appreciate the quick turnaround — we want to align timelines so your EU launch and APAC readiness meet your Q1 roadmap.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments referenced: BH-capacity-sow-draft.xlsx (draft SOW), eu-apac-topology.png (proposed routing)

From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@blueharborhealth.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: BlueHarbor Procurement <procurement@blueharborhealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-30T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: BlueHarbor — EU launch + APAC warm-standby and capacity addendum

Sergio — thanks for the summary. A few quick clarifications from procurement/infra: 

- EU location: preference is Frankfurt (DE) for latency and regulatory familiarity, but we can accept Dublin if there are constraints.
- KMS/HSM: must support customer-managed KMS for EU primary; key rotation policy required.
- Day-1 throughput: baseline 120 rps (95th percentile), spiking to 350 rps during peak windows. Failover target (APAC): rps ~80 for first 24h after failover, then scale to 250.
- Audit/logging: we need per-token retention metadata in audit logs for 13 months and proof points for SOC2 controls.

Procurement asked for a short mutual action plan and an estimated price delta for 24-month vs 12-month commitments. Also, please include an explicit fallback policy in the addendum showing behavior if EU capacity is unavailable (e.g., traffic routed to US region vs APAC warm-standby).

Cc'ing procurement mailbox so they have context. Happy to meet Oct 5 at 09:00 PT if your team can make it.

Thanks,
Emma Jones
Director, Platform Engineering | BlueHarbor Health
emma.jones@blueharborhealth.com

I’ve attached a draft SOW that includes a 24-month pricing schedule and a section called "Geo Operating Profile" that codifies the EU primary / APAC warm-standby behavior you asked for. 

High-level rollout sequence we recommend:
1) Prep (2 weeks): KMS integration, audit evidence exchange (see attached audit-evidence-list.pdf), account-level routing rules finalized.
2) EU deployment (day 0–7): stand up EU node as primary, validate latency/throughput with smoke tests.
3) APAC warm-standby (day 7–21): seed cache and replicate KV prefixes for quick failover.
4) Failover drills (day 21–28): two planned failover drills during low-traffic windows.

Proposed meeting: Oct 5, 09:00 PT (30 min) — confirmed if that works. I will follow up with a redline addendum for procurement to review and a DocuSign packet if we get verbal signoff.

Links/attachments: see BH-capacity-sow-draft.xlsx and eu-apac-topology.png. I’ve also included a short DocuSign starter link below for the commercial addendum.

Thanks — Sergio

Subject: Re: Renewal: BlueHarbor — EU launch + APAC warm-standby and capacity addendum

Emma / Team — Ben from Solutions here with technical confirmation and some concrete numbers so procurement can model cost. Below is a concise runbook and the expected performance/behavior.

Technical summary (concise):
- EU primary (Frankfurt): provision 8 x A100-equivalent dedicated GPUs, expected steady-state 120 rps at p95 for your current workload; headroom to 350 rps with autoscaling.
- APAC warm-standby (Singapore): provision 3 x A100-equivalent for warm cache and seeding; will handle initial failover load ~80 rps and autoscale to 250 rps within 20 minutes of sustained traffic.
- KV/Prefix replication: asynchronous replication of prefix cache with TTL 24h; cold-start paths covered by continuous background prefetch for high-frequency prompts.
- Failover behavior: automated routing policy with priority order EU -> APAC -> US; in the addendum we can make fallback sequence explicit and add a failover SLO (target RTO 3 min for DNS-based routing, RTO 30s when using our regional BGP TOPO option).
- KMS: support for customer-managed KMS in EU via BYOK integration; encryption-in-transit and at-rest compliant with your policy.
- Audit logs: token-level metadata emitted to your secure S3 bucket in EU and replicated to your audit workspace; retention configurable (we'll set to 13 months by default per your ask).

Attachments included: BH-capacity-sow-draft.xlsx (sizing + pricing), eu-apac-topology.png (network diagram), audit-evidence-list.pdf (SOC2 artifact checklist).

Operational notes / proposed windows:
- EU deploy: target non-business hours Oct 16–17; will require a 2-hour maintenance window for traffic cutover.
- APAC seeding: Oct 18–21, no customer-impact expected.
- Failover drills: Oct 25 and Nov 8 (both 02:00–03:00 PT).

Next steps:
1) Procurement: review the attached SOW (line-item pricing in tab 2) and confirm whether the 24-month term premium is acceptable.
2) Legal: if we get verbal signoff, Sergio will circulate the redline + DocuSign link for signature.
3) BlueHarbor infra: confirm KMS details (vendor & key-id) so we can prepare IAM/KMS integration.

Happy to take a short call during your Oct 5 slot to walk through the runbook.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
